title: Effect of defects and 3d transition-metal doping on gas adsorption in 2D silicene quantum dots: a combined DFT and machine-learning approach
content: The effects of Si vacancies and 3d transition-metal doping on gas adsorption and the multifunctional properties of silicene quantum dots (SiQDs) were investigated using density functional theory (DFT) and machine learning. Among H2S, NH3, and NO2, NO2 exhibited the strongest adsorption on pristine SiQD. Ni doping combined with a Si vacancy enhanced the adsorption energy from −0.61 to −2.11 eV, accompanied by increased charge transfer to NO2. Defects and Ni doping also modified the electronic structure, magnetic moments, and polarization-dependent optical response. Thermoelectric properties exhibited substantial variations with chemical potential. CGCNN predictions revealed configuration-dependent mechanical trends, which were further examined through DFT deformation-energy calculations. These findings demonstrate that defect and dopant engineering can effectively tune gas adsorption and the electronic, magnetic, optical, thermoelectric, and mechanical properties of SiQDs, highlighting their potential for gas-sensing and optoelectronic applications.
